title: High-throughput microfluidic cell sorting platform (MICS)
protocol: Spin coat epoxy on 100mm soda lime glass wafers.
Clamp Metglas 2714A foil to wafer overnight.
Take wafers to cleanroom.
Rinse wafers with acetone, then IPA, then dry with N2 and bake at 95°C for 5min.
Spin coat (300RPM, 20sec) MCC 80/20 primer.
Bake for 2min at 95°C.
Spin coat (500RPM 10sec, 2000RPM, 30sec) S1811 photoresist.
Prebake at 95°C for 3min.
Hard contact exposure of first mask, 150 mJ/cm², i-line.
Develop with MF 312 developer for 30sec, rinse with water.
Etch with Metglas etchant (HCl:H2O2:H2O, 1:4:23) for approximately 8min or until guides are well defined. Pipette bubbles away during etching.
Strip remaining resist with AZ300T, rinse in fresh stripper, then acetone, then IPA, N2 dry.
Dehydrate wafer at 115°C for 3min.
Spin coat Omnicoat (500RPM 5sec, 3000RPM 30sec).
Bake at 115°C for 2min.
Spin coat SU-8 3010 photoresist at 1000RPM for 30 seconds.
Prebake the sample at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Soft contact expose the second mask with 200 mJ/cm² using i-line light.
Post-exposure bake by ramping from 65°C to 95°C, hold for 3 minutes then cool gently.
Develop in SU-8 developer for 45 seconds.
Hard bake by ramping from 65°C to 150°C, hold for 15 minutes then cool gently.
Spin coat SU-8 3050 at 500RPM for 10 seconds and then at 1000RPM for 45 seconds.
Prebake the sample at 95°C for 1 hour.
Soft contact expose the third mask with 250 mJ/cm² using i-line light.
Post-exposure bake by ramping from 65°C to 95°C, hold for 6 minutes then cool gently.
Develop in SU-8 developer for 6 minutes.
Take wafers out of the cleanroom.
Dice wafers using a dicing saw.
Cast PDMS slabs, ensuring they are the same size as diced devices and set on glass slides to ensure surface smoothness. Cure in a 70°C oven overnight.
Punch holes for inlets and outlets in the PDMS slabs.
Plasma treat the PDMS in a vacuum plasma chamber for 45 seconds.
Place treated PDMS into a 10% v/v APTES:DI water solution for 30 minutes.
Rinse with DI water and dry using nitrogen gas.
Place the treated PDMS onto devices, apply weight, and put them in a 70°C oven overnight.
Trypsinize cells using 125% trypsin and wash with PBS.
Resuspend cells in HBSS supplemented with 2% BSA at a concentration of 10^7 cells/ml.
Count cells and measure viability using an automated cell counter.
Fix cells using 4% v/v PFA/PBS for 15 min at room temperature or 90% v/v ice-cold methanol/PBS added drop-wise and incubate on ice for 30 min.
Permeabilize cell plasma membrane using 0.5% Triton-X-100/PBS for 12 min at room temperature.
Block cells in 1% v/v FBS/PBS for 30 min.
Label cells with biotinylated primary antibody as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Wash cells three times in blocking buffer (2% v/v BSA/HBSS).
Remove supernatant from cells.
Resuspend cells in 80 μl of blocking buffer.
Add 20 μl of anti-biotin microbeads (sufficient for 10 million cells).
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min.
Resuspend cells in degassed sorting buffer.
Degass buffer by putting it in an Erlenmeyer flask under vacuum for 30 minutes.
The day before sorting, fill chips with 1% m/v Pluronic® F-108 in DI water and leave overnight.
Remove plunger from two 10ml syringes per chip and place them in a stand.
Label one syringe as “sample” and the other as “sheath”.
Connect one inlet tube from the chip to the “sheath” syringe, allowing pressure to backfill the “sheath” syringe with degassing solution.
Once the “sheath” syringe is filled, remove the inlet tube from the degassing set-up.
Add 20 cm of PTFE tubing and connect it to the “sample” syringe.
Allow the height of the buffer in each syringe to equalize.
Remove most of the degassing solution from both syringes, leaving a small amount to prevent air entry into the chip.
Fill with degassed sorting buffer and allow it to flow through the system, flushing out all degassing solution.
Place a 20ml, 10ml, and 3ml syringe in Chemyx syringe pump.
Add luer-lock fittings to the syringes.
Ensure the syringes are fully depressed.
Select withdraw mode on the pump.
Choose the 20ml syringe in the pump menu.
Set the desired flow rate.
Connect outlet tubing to the outlet syringes.
Attach the tube on the outside of the chip to the 3ml syringe.
Connect the inside-most tubing to the 20ml syringe.
Run the pump for 2 minutes to remove air from the tubing.
Place the chip on top of the magnet, centered over the magnetic guides.
Use double-sided tape to secure the chip in place.
Clamp the “sample” syringe.
Remove sorting buffer and add cell solution.
Tap syringes to dislodge any bubbles on the sidewalls or luer-lock fittings.
Ensure that the levels of “sample” and “sheath” fluid in the inlet columns are at the same height.
Press start on all pumps.
Check inlet column heights remain constant during operation.
Continue monitoring for air bubbles within the chips.
Allow chips to run until air bubbles appear inside them.
Clamp outlet tubing to stop individual chips.
Disconnect tubing from all outlet syringes once all chips are finished.
Label a 15 ml falcon tube for each outlet syringe and weigh it.
Transfer contents of each outlet syringe into its corresponding labeled falcon tube.
Weigh the falcon tubes again after transferring the fluid.
Take a small (10 µl) sample from each tube for automated cell counting and viability measurement.
Use remaining cells for future purposes depending on the application of this platform.
Calculate the efficiency of each chip (percentage of cells in each outlet).
Calculate the recovery (total cells collected/total cells in sample * 100%).
Ensure the efficiency matches previous sorting or flow cytometry experiments.
Confirm the desired effect is seen, such as a higher percentage in low outlet for CRISPR KO screen.
Verify cell recovery is greater than 90%.
